articles.title: The Ultimate Advent Calendar for Jet-Setters: Artist Laila Gohar's Chocolate-Filled Creation Is Inspired by 24 Luxury Destinations
articles.summary: Egyptian artist Laila Gohar is putting her characteristically whimsical spin on a holiday tradition this year, teaming up with The Luxury Collection on a limited-edition advent calendar that takes its design and culinary cues from 24 destinations around the world. The $218 calendar, available through The Luxury Collection Boutique in the U.S. and Gohar World […]
articles.content:
Egyptian artist Laila Gohar is putting her characteristically whimsical spin on a holiday tradition this year, teaming up with The Luxury Collection on a limited-edition advent calendar that takes its design and culinary cues from 24 destinations around the world.

The $218 calendar, available through The Luxury Collection Boutique in the U.S. and Gohar World in select international markets, brings together the talents of illustrator Joana Avillez and Mexican chocolatier Casa Bosques. Designed to resemble the elaborate façade of a grand hotel, the collectible features 24 numbered drawers, each housing a custom chocolate inspired by one of the hotel group's properties. Related Stories How Netflix and the NFL Hope to Establish New Thanksgiving Eve Tradition With Game and U2 Half-Time Show: ‘We Want to Create Those Global Water Cooler Moments’ ‘Virgin River’ Renewed for Season 9 to Become Netflix’s Longest-Running Original Scripted Series

Casa Bosques founder Rafael Prieto worked with culinary teams across The Luxury Collection's portfolio to develop the 24 distinct flavors, which include saffron inspired by Dubai, black sesame by Kyoto, toasted coconut by South Caicos and banana and sea salt by Waikiki. Other destinations are represented by hazelnut praline (Paris) and smoked mesquite (Los Cabos).

“I love the anticipation of opening an advent calendar, especially during the holidays,” Gohar said in a statement. “Each drawer is a small world of its own, inspired by the flavors, traditions, and details that make destinations so special at this time of year. I hope each discovery sparks curiosity and joy.”

The artist, whose eponymous homewares label Gohar World specializes in surrealist interpretations of traditional tabletop objects, has made a name for herself turning food into elaborate, often fantastical installations.

As part of the collaboration, Gohar has also designed a series of holiday pop-ups modeled after old-world Parisian chocolate shops and Milanese apothecaries. The installations feature theatrical display windows and rows of drawers that echo the design of the calendar itself. At Paris' Prince de Galles hotel, artist and set designer Alix Bortoli created bespoke vitrines incorporating the raw ingredients used in the chocolates.

The pop-ups will run throughout the holiday season at Prince de Galles in Paris, The Joseph in Nashville, Solaz in Los Cabos and The Laurus in Singapore. Select properties will also host culinary and design programming tied to the collaboration.

The partnership is part of The Luxury Collection's ongoing World in Season initiative, which highlights the culinary and cultural traditions across the Marriott-owned brand's portfolio of more than 135 hotels and resorts in 41 countries and territories.

The limited-edition Laila Gohar x The Luxury Collection advent calendar retails for $218 and is available to purchase online and at participating hotels.

articles.summary: Image courtesy of Marvel Studios Avengers: Doomsday will be here in a matter of weeks, and now, Robert Downey Jr. may just have teased that the character MCU fans most want to see in the film is officially coming. Discussions about Wanda Maximoff's eventual return to the MCU have been ongoing since the moment she died in Doctor Strange in […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Avengers: Doomsday will be here in a matter of weeks, and now, Robert Downey Jr. may just have teased that the character MCU fans most want to see in the film is officially coming. Discussions about Wanda Maximoff's eventual return to the MCU have been ongoing since the moment she died in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness . Although her return was far from confirmed, fans never lost hope, and finally, in the post-credits scene of VisionQuest , she was confirmed to be alive once again in the franchise, with Doctor Doom coming to "collect" her in the same way that he had with Bruce Banner in one of the bonus scenes in Avengers: Endgame Encore .

Specifically, Doom told Scarlet Witch that her power would be his, signaling that she would be playing a role in Doomsday , considering that is when he will first be taking on the Avengers. However, that wasn't certain; it remained possible that we wouldn't see the Scarlet Witch's return on the big screen until Avengers: Secret Wars . Now, though, following a hilarious Instagram post from Robert Downey Jr. himself, it seems Wanda will be appearing alongside Doom in Doomsday . Check out Downey's post and more about what this might mean below.

Downey took to Instagram this morning with a hilarious image in which Doom is trying to set up a seating chart for Thanksgiving. While this could be passed off as being all in good fun, and it is certainly funny, it seems likely that there is more too this. And, what makes that particularly exciting is not only the fact that Wanda's name is included but also her location on the chart right next to Doctor Doom. Particularly given that Sue Storm is also seated next to Doom, this suggests that Wanda will be crucial in the story—and that is exactly what Wanda fans are going to want to hear.

View this post on Instagram There are some other notable inclusions on this image as well. For example, behind Doom's finger, it looks like the name "Peter" is being obscured. This could mean that Doctor Doom has Peter Parker/Spider-Man as well, supporting a theory following the post-credits scene of Spider-Man: Brand New Day , in which Spider-Man is shown as being in space. Additionally, names like Loki and Bruce are included, the former of which may confirm that Loki and Doom will be directly facing off against one another (which would be thrilling) and the other reinforcing that Bruce/Hulk is going to be a key part of Doom's plan, which comes as no surprise, given his raw power.

If anything, this image just serves to make excitement for Doomsday even higher, which is yet another major boost for the film following on the heels of the final trailer being released earlier this week and a brand-new teaser appearing yesterday.

articles.title: Mario Kart World Update Adds 8 New Tracks and Other Big Upgrades, Full Patch Notes Revealed
articles.summary: Nintendo has released a new update for Mario Kart World today and it happens to be one of the game's largest so far in 2026. Over the past year, Switch 2 owners have loudly made it known that they want Nintendo to release new content, whether it be paid or free, for Mario Kart World. […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Nintendo has released a new update for Mario Kart World today and it happens to be one of the game's largest so far in 2026. Over the past year, Switch 2 owners have loudly made it known that they want Nintendo to release new content, whether it be paid or free, for Mario Kart World . And while Nintendo has released some new additions to the game in the wake of these requests, none of these content drops have been very substantial. Now, Nintendo is trying to rectify this just a bit with today's new update, but it still might not satisfy some fans.

Downloadable now, update version 1.9.0 for Mario Kart World most notably brings eight new tracks to the game. While this is somewhat of a major deal for MKW , it's worth noting that none of these courses are wholly original. Instead, they're merely remixed versions of tracks that have already been in the game. So a course like "Koopa Troopa Beach" now simply has a new iteration called "Koopa Troopa Beach 2" that players can experience, and so on. As a result, Nintendo still has yet to add any wholly new tracks to Mario Kart World , which will undoubtedly continue to prompt requests from players.

Outside of these new tracks, this Mario Kart World update does a handful of other things. Along with squashing a handful of bugs players have been discovering, this patch also introduces two new paths for Knockout Tour. This, in addition to a new replay option, represents the most prominent changes that Nintendo has made with this update to MKW .

articles.title: Netflix As The New Cable: From Friend To Foe To Friend Again, How Streamer Became Go-To Source Of Off-Network Revenue & Tune-In Promotion
articles.summary: Initially welcomed by legacy media companies as an additional revenue stream for library content to offset the declines in DVD sales, third-party streamers, particularly Netflix, have evolved into a replacement for the depressed off-network syndication business and a viable promotional platform to drum up interest for new season launches on broadcast — and beyond. articles.content:
Initially welcomed by legacy media companies as an additional revenue stream for library content to offset the declines in DVD sales, third-party streamers, particularly Netflix , have evolved into a replacement for the depressed off-network syndication business and a viable promotional platform to drum up interest for new season launches on broadcast — and beyond.

The latest example is the major film and TV licensing deal Netflix recently made with Disney. It includes multi-year agreements for drama Will Trent and comedy Shifting Gears , whose existing seasons are launching on the streamer weeks ahead of their upcoming season premieres on ABC. The latter debuted on Netflix earlier this month and is projected to crack the Nielsen Top 10 when the next ranking is released. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories News UK Actors Union Equity To Kickstart Negotiations With Streamers Early Next Year Sports NFL Thanksgiving Week Football Schedule: How To Watch & Livestream All Games

Disney has first-hand experience how a streaming window on Netflix can help a broadcast series via its pioneering at the time pact for ABC drama Grey's Anatomy, which made its debut on the platform in 2015 . Making previous seasons available on the streamer has recruited a new generation of fans for the medical drama, extending the series' life on ABC where it is currently airing its 23rd season. The breakthrough came four years prior when the success of AMC's Breaking Bad on Netflix helped the series avoid cancellation and become an award-winning hit for the cable network, prompting creator Vince Gilligan to give the streamer credit for keeping Breaking Bad on the air following the first of two Outstanding Drama Series Emmy wins in 2013.

Soon, there was a name for that — "the Riverdale phenomenon" — after the 2017 CW series which delivered OK, not spectacular ratings during its first season on the network before exploding on Netflix over the summer, leading to a ratings surge for the following season on the CW that fall.

"After that, everyone was like, 'Oh, I want my show on Netflix because then everyone will watch it,'" one industry veteran recalled.

Still, Netflix's output with the CW that Riverdale was part of notwithstanding, major library streaming pacts for on-air broadcast/basic cable series made after their first season were not that common, with NBC's The Blacklist and Blindspot , Fox's New Girl , Gotham and Lucifer and TNT's Animal Kingdom as notable examples, all selling in competitive situations. (Of the six, The Blacklist, New Girl and Gotham went to Netflix, Blindspot and Lucifer were acquired by Hulu before Lucifer became a Netflix original, Animal Kingdom by Prime Video.) blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

NBC's Good Girls was another streaming success story on Netflix. Licensed under an old co-production model Netflix employed in the late 2010s, its first season made its debut on Netflix in the U.S. on Jan. 1, 2019, just two months before the Season 2 launch on NBC. The series' success on Netflix and the generous fees coming from the streamer helped keep Good Girls on the air for four seasons despite declining linear ratings.

While lucrative for the studios, such third-party licensing agreements largely dried up when legacy media companies started launching their own streamers in 2019-20 and initially kept virtually of their series in a walled garden. That has gradually changed, with Netflix carrying more current ABC, NBC, CBS and Fox series than ever. (While Netflix has been dominating the field, there are rare exceptions with other third-party streamers, like CBS' Ghosts being available on Prime Video.)

What has evolved from the early-days exclusive SVOD pacts is that third-party deals now are largely not exclusive: the broadcast series are available on their sibling streamers which have both in-season (next day) and out-of-season (previous seasons) rights, while Netflix and other third-party streamers get the shows out-of-season, launching a season after it has finished its broadcast run.

That is in line with how syndication worked, though the streamer is getting new broadcast series much faster than the traditional model where shows had to make it to four seasons and 100 episodes to launch in syndication, first on local broadcast stations and then on cable.

"Then cable and local markets collapsed on top of each other, and eventually streaming essentially took the place of this syndication window. But not after four years, after one year," one industry veteran said.

Network series are now commonly sold to third-party platforms after their first season for an SVOD window that has two main entry points: a season dropping on the streamer 30 days after the season finale had been released, which shows such as Grey's Anatomy and the the CW's Sullivan's Crossing adhere to on Netflix, or at the start of the next broadcast season.

The latter was the case with New Girl and The Blacklist and is currently in play with NBC comedies Happy's Place and St. Denis Medical as well as Fox drama Doc , all on Netflix. In many cases, the fall entry point has evolved into a streaming season launch 30 or so days prior to the start of the next season on broadcast, providing an opportunity for people to get back into a show by catching up and reengaging.

That makes for strategic deployments like this fall's Netflix premieres of ABC's Will Trent and Shifting Gears timed to the next seasons' debut on broadcast with a strong promotional purpose. ( Will Trent dropped on Netflix two months ahead of the series' return on ABC, for Shifting Gears , the lead-in is about 30 days.)

Fox's Best Medicine and Animal Control — both owned by the network — also launch their previous season on Netflix a month ahead of the new seasons debuting on Fox.

Meanwhile, CBS' Fire Country is adding a wrinkle by going back an extra season. Its first season released on Netflix about two months ahead of its Season 3 premiere on CBS in 2024, and Season 2 made its Netflix debut about two months ahead of Season 4 debut on CBS in 2025. Interestingly, Fire Country 's presence on Netflix has been limited to these two seasons, with newer seasons only available on CBS sibling Paramount+. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

One of the earliest examples of such use of Netflix after the broadcast networks already had streamers in the corporate family was a one-year non-exclusive licensing deal CBS Studios made in September 2020 to put the first seasons of drama Evil and comedy The Unicorn on Netflix ahead of the premiere of their second seasons on CBS.

The stunt didn't help the Walton Goggins comedy, which was canceled by after two seasons. (The same happened to NBC's The Hunting Party despite a strong Season 1 launch on Netflix a little over a month into The Hunting Party 's second season on NBC.)

Meanwhile, Evil 's strong sampling on Netflix helped inform the decision to move the supernatural drama from CBS to Paramount+. The series' streaming performance also likely factored into the initial one-year non-exclusive licensing deal with Netflix getting extended to five years and the show's first three seasons.

The way streaming launches are plotted by series' owners is in line with the function basic cable served in its heyday for shows sold in off-network syndication whose latest season would become available on cable in September, just before the next season starts airing on broadcast.

To further promote a series' return on broadcast, shows used to do marathons on cable. What is a TV marathon's equivalent in the streaming era? Binging — or dropping the entire previous season on a platform like Netflix ahead of the new one's network premiere.

Exposure is great but it doesn't pay the bills — at least not directly — so the proliferation of Netflix licensing deals has been fueled by other motives too as networks and studios grapple with declines in linear ratings and the ad revenue attached to them.

"There is enhanced promotion, but also economics are driving these things," one industry insider said. "Studios are carrying deficits on these shows, they need to find revenue, so because because the four-year syndication window really is not there anymore, they have to find revenue."

For studios, the latter sometimes takes precedent. "From our standpoint, we're going to look at the money first, and then the marketing aspect second," one studio executive said.

The decisions are made with many factors in mind, including profit participants who get a portion of off-network revenue.

Talent agents who represent creatives have been lamenting the demise of the off-network syndication model, claiming that the money from streaming deals doesn't come close to the syndication windfall in covering shows' deficits and paying profit participants, with proceeds also down from the early days of the streaming wars when Netflix was paying premium for (predominantly exclusive) SVOD rights.

Studio executives argue that money is still there for the taking, but instead of one syndication revenue stream, there are multiple steaming ones as the era of large audiences watching network shows in syndication five days a week is gone. Now viewership is fractured, and so are streaming deals, non-exclusive over a myriad of platforms.

"Our business is not just streaming to the big ones, Netflix and Amazon; it's also AVOD, it's Roku and Tubi. There's multiple ways you can now make money, which is great," one TV executive said. "In the aggregate for individual shows probably will rarely get close to what a show could have made in its peak syndication days, so agents probably see that more than we do because they're focusing on the individual performance of one show in its U.S. life cycle." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

Exactly six years after the Riverdale phenomenon, in the summer of 2023, we had the Suits phenomenon when an old USA Network series became the biggest show in America, breaking a slew of streaming ratings records and amassing eye-popping 57.7 billion minutes watched for the year despite only launching on Netflix U.S. in June.

It showed that cable series, once thought to be of no off-network syndication value, can draw big numbers when exposed to a new, wide audience on streaming.

That carried over to pay cable too, with Starz's biggest series, Outlander and Power, and Showtime's signature shows Dexter, Homeland, Shameless and Yellowjackets finding their way to Netflix, many of the deals driven by the series' producing studios.

With the dire state of the linear TV business, for basic cable networks that want to stay in the original scripted programming — and some pay cable ones too — a syndication-type deal with a major streamer is a do-or-die, a crucial revenue stream that allows them to afford scripted series.

That explains the big new $500 million licensing deal AMC recently made with Netflix for the entire The Walking Dead universe. Ever since Breaking Bad 's Netflix breakthrough, AMC has been licensing its biggest originals to the streamer, including The Walking Dead mothership for almost 15 years and Anne Rice's Immortal Universe, the newer ones shared with its own platform AMC+.

Meanwhile, Disney's FX is essentially a streaming brand on Hulu, delivering some of the platform's biggest hits, like American Horror Story, Love Story: John F. Kennedy Jr. & Carolyn Bessette, Shōgun , and The Bear .

In January, Netflix announced a deal with Paramount for 20 series, which, surprisingly, included a Taylor Sheridan Paramount+ original, Mayor of Kingstown .

HBO had previously licensed some of its originals to Netflix years after they had ended their run, including Sex and the City, Band of Brothers and Six Feet Under, with marquee series such as The Sopranos and Game of Thrones off limits. In contrast, Mayor of Kingstown is a current original on a rival streamer, part of Paramount+'s treasured Taylorverse. The other titles in the package are largely former CBS series, along with Matlock , licensed to Netflix only internationally.

I hear Mayor of Kingstown was a late addition as Netflix was not willing to take the other titles without it. I hear the Mayor of Kingstown producers leveraged the series' inclusion to get an extra season as Paramount+ had planned to end the show after Season 4. A renewal for an abbreviated fifth and final season was announced just days before the Netflix licensing deal, which includes the first four seasons of Mayor of Kingstown , was unveiled.

In May, David Ellison, then-CEO of Paramount, now co-CEO of Skydance, told Wall Street analysts that the company will continue to license select programming to third parties “for the foreseeable future.”

Amazon similarly made a Netflix deal for the first three seasons of MGM+'s acclaimed but not widely known sci-fi horror drama From, which has released four seasons and has been renewed for a fifth and final season. It has turned into a Suits/Riverdale -style phenomenon, amassing more than 5 billion minutes viewed in the U.S. in its first three weeks. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

As part of its Netflix licensing deal, Disney took a step further by lending a top Disney+ original series in its prime, Percy Jackson and the Olympians , for an unprecedented short, three-month window, along with the Ice Age movie franchise. The stunt is timed to the release of the new season of Percy Jackson on Disney+ on Nov. 20 and the new Ice Age movie, Boiling Point, on Feb. 5, 2027.

Touting the mutual benefits of the deal for Disney and Netflix, the latter's co-CEO Ted Sarandos joked about plugging rival Disney's Ice Age: Boiling Point on the streamer's earnings call last month, name-checking his Disney counterpart Josh D'Amaro by quipping, "You're welcome, Josh."

"We expect to have opportunities throughout for the best series and the best films with all the suppliers," Sarandos said about the Netflix licensing strategy. "It's a little complicated because all of our suppliers are also our competitors. Our deals bring in much needed revenue. They certainly build awareness, and the benefit of that awareness transfers back to them because it helps grow the value of their IP. So these deals really are win-win."

articles.title: 5 PlayStation Black Friday Deals You Won't Want to Miss Before November 2026 Ends
articles.summary: Courtesy of Sony With Black Friday approaching, PlayStation players will want to take advantage of several deals on some big games, including a few exclusives that are finally being marked at lower prices. From celebrated titles getting a sequel soon to some familiar hits of the past year, there are many different deals to choose from, offering dozens […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google With Black Friday approaching, PlayStation players will want to take advantage of several deals on some big games, including a few exclusives that are finally being marked at lower prices. From celebrated titles getting a sequel soon to some familiar hits of the past year, there are many different deals to choose from, offering dozens to hundreds of hours of gameplay within certain titles. That being said, the Black Friday 2026 deals for PlayStation only last until November 30, so you'll want to grab whatever games you can quickly before they expire.

Some games in the Black Friday deals for PlayStation include some titles that are only dropping slightly in price, but that may be just enough for some players to purchase them. Games like Control Resonant and Baldur's Gate 3 are only knocking off a few dollars from their standard price, while other games like Resident Evil Requiem have made their Deluxe edition cost as much as the base version of the title. While not the greatest deals PlayStation is offering for the holiday season, they are still worth mentioning, as many players did not expect games of those caliber to be put on sale at all.

One of the most recent exclusives for the PlayStation 5 is Marvel's Wolverine , the Insomniac superhero title that features the six-clawed mutant from many X-Men stories. This action-adventure game is set within its own universe, telling a unique story with various X-Men characters and featuring hack-and-slash gameplay for players to get lost in. While this game hasn't been the recipient of as many accolades as Insomniac's Marvel's Spider-Man series, Marvel's Wolverine is still a gorgeous looking game with satisfying combat.

Currently, PlayStation has Marvel's Wolverine 's Standard Edition on sale for $49.69, marking around a 30% price decrease from its typical $69.99 cost. The game is a single-player adventure, meaning that it doesn't have as much play time as other titles, but multiple difficulty modes and combat challenges does add replayability to the game. The intense, gritty, M-rated combat of Marvel's Wolverine is very different compared to Marvel's Spider-Man , giving players more lethal action to sink their teeth into. For that reason, this can be a great title to pick up on Black Friday, but it isn't the only game on sale to feature Wolverine.

With the announcement of Robert Pattinson playing the next iteration of James Bond in Denis Villeneuve's upcoming 007 movie, perhaps players will be interested in trying 007 First Light . This game was developed by IO Interactive, the creators behind the modern Hitman series, with gameplay heavily reflecting the espionage and infiltration mechanics of that franchise. However, part of the charm of 007 First Light comes from a charming, excellent performance of James Bond by actor Patrick Gibson, whose depiction of the iconic spy has earned him a 2026 Game Award nomination.

Black Friday deals have marked down 007 First Light 50% of its original price, knocking it from $69.99 to $34.99. This is one of the best reviewed games of the year, featuring a unique story about Bond in his early years of becoming a legendary MI6 spy. Clever level design creates large sandboxes for players to tackle goals in whatever way they please, providing non-linear segments that reward ingenuity. Much like the adaptability of James Bond himself, players have to find ways to improvise and adjust plans to different situations, completing missions through suave cunning rather than brute force.

The little details of 007 First Light are what make it such an excellent Bond experience, from James' one-liner dialogue whenever he's caught somewhere he shouldn't be to the flashing "License to Kill" marker on screen when players are authorized to get violent. Solid gunplay mixes with classic Q gadgets to make this feel like the closest game to a James Bond movie since 007 GoldenEye , a landmark game. With various difficulty modes to increase replayability too, this Black Friday deal holds incredible value to fans of the 007 franchise.

Madden NFL 27 is listed on sale for $34.99, marking it down 50% from the Standard Edition's normal price of $69.99. The latest iteration of the football simulation Madden series, this title is perhaps the most visually impressive of the franchise yet, with hyper-realistic gameplay and graphics mirroring the sport its based on closely. Dynamic physics combine with game-changing weather mechanics to create one of the more immersive Madden games to come out recently. In an era where GTA 6 is redefining what high-quality realism looks like in games, Madden 27 is a great title that reflects that direction.

Madden 27 isn't without its problems with monetization and live service features that have plagued sports games over the years, but it is marginally better than College Football 27 's situation. In fact, the large price drop for the Standard Edition of Madden 27 makes in-game purchases more manageable for players who want to build a dynamic team to use online, especially while hype surrounding the 2026-27 football season continues. With a new roster of players with changed stats from the previous year, grabbing Madden 27 before Super Bowl LXI (Super Bowl 61) might be the right move.

The first Halo game to ever come to PlayStation consoles is Halo: Campaign Evolved , a remake of the classic Combat Evolved released in 2001. Campaign Evolved makes a lot of changes to the original title, adding gameplay elements from modern Halo games like Halo Infinite into the remake, such as new weapons, sprinting, and other features. While this can be alienating to older fans, new PlayStation players might appreciate the changes, as they relate to other shooters on Sony systems better, therefore allowing them to jump into Campaign Evolved with fewer obstacles.

Halo: Campaign Evolved is currently listed for $29.99 instead of $49.99, taking the game down 40% for PlayStation players. This title not only recreates all of the main story levels of Combat Evolved with new cutscenes and higher visual fidelity, but also adds three new prequel missions never seen in the classic sci-fi FPS before. In addition, free updates for the game plan to expand its multiplayer, adding classic modes like the PvE Firefight for many players to jump into together. With other never-before-seen features like a third-person POV, Halo: Campaign Evolved is a solid introduction to the series, despite lacking the franchise's competitive online PvP multiplayer.

The other big Marvel game sale going on for Black Friday is for Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls , the 4v4 fighting game made by Arc System Works, the developers behind other great games like Dragon Ball FighterZ and Guilty Gear Strive . This game is being listed at $39.59 for its base edition, taking it down 34% of its base price for players to pick it up before December 1, 2026. This game is one of the most complete fighting game releases of the year, having a strong 20 character roster comprised of different teams of characters, including:

Players can take control any of these characters in teams of four, with each fighter having incredibly deep move lists that reflect their unique powers and skill sets from Marvel Comics. The game features a robust story mode focused on any of the above teams as they try to face off against The Champion, a powerful cosmic entity looking for the universe's strongest fighters. Written by actual comic writers, the surprisingly deep story content in this game is on par with other fighting games like Mortal Kombat , which are known for weaving interesting narratives into their single-player experiences.

That being said, the online matchmaking of this title is solid too, giving players chances to join lobbies and participate in casual or ranked matches with their teams. Other modes like Survival offer roguelike challenges to unlock character outfits, giving players ways to play for various rewards besides the daunting task of facing others online. Although this PlayStation sale doesn't give players new DLC characters like Phoenix Cyclops, it does represent a great introduction to one of the best fighting games of the year for Black Friday.

What games will you be picking up on PlayStation for Black Friday? Let us know in the comments below!

Netflix is the only major industry player not currently funding the UK's anonymous whistleblowing service for complaints about bullying and harassment, it has been revealed.

The Creative Industries Independent Standards Authority ( CIISA ) has released its long-expected list of funders and the streamer's absence is notable, along with a number of talent agencies.

Last year, a Deadline analysis found that Channel 4, Disney and Amazon were among those refusing to pay annual CIISA fees, while at the time Netflix and Skydance (then Paramount) declined to confirm if they were providing support. UK Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy , a vocal backer of CIISA, has also previously chided MasterChef producer Banijay for the same thing. Today's register shows Channel 4, Disney, Amazon, Skydance and Banijay are now all paying, along with other production groups and major broadcasters plus Sky. Spike in reports since Brand & Walliams

CIISA received 90 anonymous reports between its June launch and November 20, the body said today. Notably, we understand nearly half of these reports came during the two weeks after Brand was convicted and the Walliams allegations were published.

Emerging from the Time's Up UK movement and Noel Clarke allegations, CIISA has taken years to get up and running but is now a fully-fledged indepedent whistleblowing service. As an officially designated whistleblowing body, people can anonymously report concerns to CIISA relating to harassment, discrimination, victimisation and other harmful practices. CIISA can then signpost help, make lawful refererals, generate reports and identify issues, themes and patterns.

In parliament today, CIISA gathered bigwigs like Nandy, BBC chair Samir Shah, ex-BBC Director General Tim Davie and Zelda Perkins, the Harvey Weinstein victim who campaigns on outlawing NDAs. In a discussion chaired by Sky News Presenter Cathy Newman, attendees discussed ongoing challenges within the creative industries and efforts to drive improvements in workplace culture.

CIISA boss Jen Smith said: "CIISA has a pivotal role to play in preventing harm and closing accountability gaps in the creative industry infrastructure, offering a unique opportunity to identify harmful patterns of behaviour across different projects. We thank the organisations who have already pledged their support for this important work and we will continue to work alongside industry and government to ensure that CIISA is adequately resourced to offer a safe, confidential route for people to seek independent advice and report concerns, and to embed the consistent cross-sector standards that will drive lasting change.”

“Green Lava,” an inspirational Vatican -produced documentary short in the running for the Oscars , has unveiled its new global trailer which features Justin Bieber ’s song “Everything Hallelujah.” The doc follows a 22-year-old Italian man named Giacomo Mattivi, who lives with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.

Use of Bieber’s “Everything Hallelujah” was secured through a licensing agreement with Universal Music Enterprises, a division of UMG Recordings, Inc., following an introduction facilitated by music manager Daniel Weissman, according to a statement. "The song's themes of faith and gratitude echo Giacomo's outlook on life and the documentary's exploration of family, perseverance and hope," the statement noted. Financial terms were not disclosed. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'Dune: Prophecy' Star Tabu Joins YRF Entertainment's Netflix Rescue Drama 'Tunnel Men' (EXCLUSIVE) Kevin Kline Reunites With Meryl Streep in 'The Corrections' Series at Netflix

As previously reported by Variety , "Green Lava" marks the first time in the Academy Awards' 97-year history that the Vatican has submitted a film for Oscar consideration. That said, the film will not specifically represent the Vatican in the race. Unlike the international feature film category, short films do not need an official submission or endorsement from a national government or a country-specific committee.

The 39-minute doc, which is set against the breathtaking backdrop of the Dolomites, is directed by Lia Beltrami and Ali Aksu. "Green Lava" follows Giacomo “as he faces life without his brother Mattia who has just succumbed to Duchenne,” says the film’s synopsis.

"From university lectures and football matches with friends to running a small egg-selling business and spending time with family, Giacomo embraces life with remarkable determination," according to promotional materials, which add: "Defying societal expectations, Giacomo challenges the limitations imposed by his condition and finds strength in his community and in the natural world that surrounds him.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“We chose 'Everything Hallelujah' because Justin matches the color and emotional frequency of 'Green Lava' so precisely," said its co-directors Beltrami and Aksu in a statement to Variety.

"The film is rooted in Giacomo's deep faith and his view of life as a blessing, and Justin carries that same spirit through his gratitude for the small details of his own life," they continued. "Giacomo wants to inspire people to embrace love and to approach death, and our transition, with honesty. It's the subject we avoid most in daily life, even though none of us knows when that moment will come. The key is finding balance: treating each day as a new blessing and staying grateful for everything God created,” they concluded.

The new trailer featuring Bieber’s “Everything Hallelujah" arrives after, earlier this month, former Amazon MGM Studios executive Glenn S. Gainor and industry veteran Sandy Climan joined "Green Lava" — via their film production outfit and consultancy Hollywood Ventures Group (HVG) — as executive producers, along with Nabeel Laher and Nelly Kim and John Shufeldt MD.

“Green Lava” completed its Oscar-qualifying theatrical run by screening between Sept. 18-24 at the Lumiere Music Hall in Beverly Hills.

More recently, a screening for Academy members was held on Nov. 8 at The London West Hollywood in Los Angeles, attended by Paolo Ruffini, who heads the Vatican’s Dicastery for Communication and representatives from the Archdiocese of Los Angeles. The dicastery for communication controls the Vatican’s television, radio, online, publishing and newspaper operations.

Upcoming “Green Lava” screenings are planned in London and New York, with the doc also set to screen during Rome’s Tertio Millennio Film Festival.

Beltrami’s company Emotions to Generate Change and Untold Production produced “Green Lava” in collaboration with Vatican News, Radio Vaticana and Vatican Media. Aksu and Beltrami serve as producers, together with Los Angeles-based David Dubinsky and Dominique Appleby. Hollywood Ventures Group also serves as an executive producing partner, with Glenn S. Ted has found new life through the success of its Peacock TV series , and now Seth MacFarlane's universe is set to expand with a new animated series keeping the franchise going. But it's taking things in a new direction that blends both the TV and movie releases.

Ted: The Animated Series picks up 12 years after the events of Ted 2 , and focuses on the older versions of John and Ted as the two of them now have wacky family adventures together. But thankfully it's brought two of the fan favorites from the TV series into the fold with a new sneak peek clip showing off Susan (Alanna Ubach) and Matty (Scott Grimes). You can check it out in action below.

Ted: The Animated Series will be making its debut with Peacock on Thursday, December 17th with eight episodes all available at once. Additional episodes of the animated series planned for a release sometime in 2027, but no concrete release date has been announced as of this time. The series is set 12 years after the events of the Ted films, and brings back its core cast with Seth MacFarlane as Ted, Mark Wahlberg as John, Amanda Seyfried as Sam, and Jessica Barth as Tami-Lynn. Kyle Mooney and Liz Richman join the cast as Apollo and Ruth, new additions to their families.

Ted: The Animated Series thankfully incorporates two of the big fan favorite changes to the Ted universe seen with the Ted TV series. Alanna Ubach and Scott Grimes' versions of John's parents are completely different than seen in the film franchise, and luckily they will be making their return to the franchise with this animated series despite it taking place within the universe of the films. But there's still a glaring absence from Giorgia Whigham’s Blaire through the promotional materials so far.

For those fans of the Ted TV series, the humor of this new animated version seems to be more in line with it. That's also helped by the fact that Ted: The Animated Series is created Seth MacFarlane, Paul Corrigan and Brad Walsh, who were also showrunners of the live-action series. It seems that while a third season of the live-action series might not be in the cards for the moment as it's been deemed too "expensive" for Peacock , the team has found a creative way to keep things going.

Ted: The Animated Series might not be the kind of continuation that fans of the Peacock series might have been hoping to see , but with Matty and Susan returning for the new adventures to blend with the movie's cast that's going to make it all the more appealing to see how the team is able to work together both worlds. articles.title: Jean Grey #1 has Marvel's Strongest Mutant Return in Glorious Fashion and an Amazing New Perspective on Her Character (Review)
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Jean Grey is, without question, one of the most powerful characters in Marvel. She's the master of and an essential part of the Phoenix Force, which is the embodiment of the very concepts of life and rebirth. The only people who could even hope to compare to Jean in terms of raw power are the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Jean Grey is, without question, one of the most powerful characters in Marvel. She's the master of and an essential part of the Phoenix Force, which is the embodiment of the very concepts of life and rebirth. The only people who could even hope to compare to Jean in terms of raw power are the highest echelon of characters, such as a full-powered Franklin Richards or Galactus. Jean is a true hero, but she's also beyond dangerous. Her most famous story is, of course, "The Dark Phoenix Saga," which saw her lose control to her powers and destroy an entire planet. Now, Jean Grey (2026) #1 has her on that path for an entirely different reason.

In the wake of DNX , Cyclops is thought to be dead , and Jean was never going to take becoming a widow lying down. After years of touring space as a cosmic protector, this mini-series is bringing Jean back to Earth in a big way. It's all about reconnecting Jean with her roots as an X-Man, and this issue is not only a fantastic transition from her cosmic era to her stay on Earth, but a wonderful character study that explores what it is that makes Jean so interesting. Even better, it also holds up a mirror to Jean and another beloved hero, the Scarlet Witch, in a way that makes me wish these two could get their own duo comic.

Jean is a difficult character to write. Or, at the very least, people who write her tend to fall into a few traps. On the one hand, you have Jean Grey as the most deeply empathetic and human of the X-Men, and on the other, you have the cosmic force of raw power known as the Phoenix. Jean as a person is incredibly down to Earth, but she's also connected to a power and mentality that's so beyond human it's nearly incomprehensible. A good Jean story will acknowledge both of these aspects and blend them together without one overpowering the other, and this is a great Jean issue.

One of its biggest strengths is how it balances Jean and the Phoenix as part of the same whole, but also distinct. They blend together, but there are also clear lines drawn. This issue is a fantastic exploration of Jean's character, taking us through her thought process as she loses the one person she loved more than anyone else, and it is also clear to call out how much is Jean and how much of her rampage is Jean losing herself to the powers of the Dark Phoenix . It's a delicate balance that gives us a wonderful window into Jean's psyche without detracting from the very physical threat she poses, which is shown off perfectly.

Speaking of characterization, Jean isn't the only one to benefit. Wanda is a fantastic parallel to Jean, being the person to pull her out of her rage by connecting to her heart instead of fighting her power. They truly have gone on similar journeys, despite never truly being on the same page before in almost any regard. This single interaction made me want an entire series, or at least a story, dissecting their dynamic as they battle cosmic horrors together, but that's a case for another time. Regardless, the emotional heart of this story is amazing, and Wanda brings it home perfectly.

Rogê Antônio is the artist for this series, with colors by Edgar Delgado and letters by Ariana Maher. Starting off with the strong points, Antônio's work with expressions in this issue is nothing short of incredible. Every character is constantly moving and shown at different angles, but their faces always tell every facet of their emotions, no matter how complicated. Some of my favorite examples are Quintein's awe and fear as Jean parts with the Phoenix, the clear tender love on Wanda's face as she kisses Vision, and Jean and Beast's grief as they stand over Cyclops's grave. The faces here tell a story all on their own.

The depiction of Jean's cosmic flames and the mind scape are also great, wich the shattering glass of both Jean's rage and the cage holding her being one in the same being fantastic. However, while the art here is good from page to page, the scale of it could definitely be amped up for Jean. The story does an amazing job of driving home just how dangerous the Dark Phoenix is, but the actual confrontation with her feels very cramped. It definitely drags down the overall impact of the fight, making the Phoenix feel small when it should feel larger than life. The art is great, but it could be more open.

Overall, this was still an incredible first issue for Jean, bringing her into a new status quo as she adjusts to life without Scott and being back on Earth. I am beyond excited to see where she goes from here. Let us know what you think about Jean's new adventure in the comments below!

articles.title: Gilles Villeneuve Biopic ‘The Rise of a Legend’ Gives Racing Genre a Grungier Spin: It’s the ‘Anti-“F1”’
articles.summary: “Villeneuve: The Rise of a Legend” director Yan Lanouette Turgeon doesn’t mince his words, saying his 1970s-set biopic of Formula 1 racer Gilles Villeneuve is the antithesis of Joseph Kosinski’s “F1,” starring Brad Pitt. His film closes Torino Film Festival next week before a wider international rollout. "We're the anti-'F1,'" he says. "We're so far […]
articles.content:
“ Villeneuve: The Rise of a Legend ” director Yan Lanouette Turgeon doesn’t mince his words, saying his 1970s-set biopic of Formula 1 racer Gilles Villeneuve is the antithesis of Joseph Kosinski’s “ F1 ,” starring Brad Pitt. His film closes Torino Film Festival next week before a wider international rollout.

"We're the anti-'F1,'" he says. "We're so far from NASA chief engineers improving aerodynamics. We're in the garage, it smells of oil, and the mechanics are shirtless, changing tires with cigarettes dangling from their lips. The manual transmission felt more symbiotic between driver and car. It wasn't a NASA driving machine but a man steering an engine. There was something romantic about that era, more rudimentary and far more dangerous." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories United Talent Agency Signs 'Steps' Filmmaker Alyce Tzue (EXCLUSIVE) Netflix’s Hit French Action Thriller ‘Elite Force’ Starring Tomer Sisley Starts Production on Season 2

Villeneuve was one of its casualties, dying in a 1982 crash after winning six Grands Prix. True to its title, this bootstraps biopic focuses instead on his improbable rise from rural obscurity in Quebec to carrying the Ferrari banner on racing’s most elite tracks.

The choice has clearly paid off. After premiering as the closing film at Toronto, "Villeneuve: The Rise of a Legend" has run laps around the Quebec box office, nearing 2 million local admissions in one of the strongest launches since 2019.

Variety caught up with the filmmaker ahead of the Turin screening.

I came in after artistic differences between the producer and the original director, and I was offered the reins. But people kept telling me stories about Gilles, or where they were when they heard he had died. I found him inspiring for his guts, perseverance and relentlessness, and I felt we need a figure like that right now. As soon as I told people I was making the film, I realized he was still very present in Quebecers' hearts, even if his public image had dimmed over the years. For many, he'd become just a racetrack, the Circuit Gilles-Villeneuve in Montreal. People assume everyone knows him because a track bears his name, but figures like him fade if no one brings them back into the conversation. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

It was a screenwriting decision from the start. You can't depict a whole life in a biopic. It becomes tiresome and directionless, so you have to choose where to land. I always liked where the film ends. The rest of his story is well documented, with many documentaries on his F1 career, but few people, even in Quebec, know the steps that got him there. His path was singular. He was a seasoned musician, and I wanted a parallel between the jazzman and his very instinctive driving style. He started in snowmobiles, then had a magical run in Formula Atlantic. It's a lesson in perseverance. It's not only a film about Gilles but about the people who helped him rise. They say it takes a village, and he's the perfect example. We end on a high note: the little guy from Berthierville landing the most coveted seat in F1.

Both men died at 32, around the same era, and both are seen as eternally young. Their sons, Brandon Lee and Jacques Villeneuve, were also seen through the lens of their fathers. And both started from nothing, clawed their way up, and became legends in their disciplines. The reference came during editing. We needed something to put on a TV in a scene, and a small Bruce Lee clip resonated with him at that moment.

Even if you don't know where Berthierville is, you understand he comes from a modest background, and you feel how much money racing demands. That's an underdog story right there. In Toronto, many people couldn't place Berthierville relative to Montreal, but they responded very well in all three screenings. There's something universal in the quest to dream big and go all in. Gilles pushed all his chips in, like a good poker player. Many young people are going, even though they never knew him. The name still resonates among racing fans in Europe, and [series like Netflix's] "Formula 1: Drive to Survive" brought many young viewers to F1. The international version may carry a "based on a true story" subtitle. We didn't need that in Quebec, but we know where it's headed. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Gilles took a very different path to becoming a driver, and that's what made him unique, even in Formula 1. You can see it in how he took corners, sliding the car to exit faster. He first showed that appetite for pushing limits on snowmobiles, which is pretty wild. When riders collide and go flying, the crashes are incredible. It was a dangerous sport, but he clearly loved the thrill. I told my lead to pay attention to how Gilles looks at people. He had a mischievous side and was always up for a prank or pushing a new vehicle to its limits. When he bought a helicopter, people who flew with him once never got back in because he'd scared them half to death. That sense of adventure was part of who he was. And snowmobiling is such a Quebecois thing. I can't wait to see how audiences react to those races.

Set the stakes before going into a race. If they're clear for the main character, the race stays relevant to the story. To contain the budget, we asked which races we needed and what each meant on Gilles' path to F1. We designed and choreographed them, even created pre-viz animations, so we knew exactly what to shoot. I wanted us to live the race with Gilles, mostly from his point of view, cutting on his gaze and staying with him through gear changes and corners, with images that could have been shot in the 1970s. Speed comes from editing and camera position: the lower the camera, the more you feel the speed and every imperfection of the track. You discover these tricks by studying what works.

Yes. Our first shot is a tribute: "Grand Prix" opens on a car's exhaust, and I thought, we'll start like that. I liked it less for its story than for how the races were shot. Frankenheimer reportedly shot more footage than almost any film in history because he was after something real. I've seen all the racing films, like "Le Mans." In research you absorb everything that's been done, put it in a box, and then find your own way to tell your story.

I did, since films like "Ford v Ferrari," "Days of Thunder," "Grand Prix" or "Le Mans" always show the protagonists' full faces. But I realized almost immediately while shooting, and fully once in the editing room, that it would work. Eyes say so much, and [lead actor] Rémi Goulet could convey emotion and relive everything even in extreme close-up. Generally, you can't be close to characters whose faces you can't see, but for us it somehow works. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Very difficult. These films are rare because they're extremely expensive, and Quebec doesn't necessarily have the means. We also have little expertise in filming action and racing, so we had to break new ground to put the viewer in the middle of the races. Sometimes it felt like making my student films with makeshift means; at other times we had far more resources than the average Quebec film. I hope more will follow, because it's worth investing in something that can resonate with audiences at home and internationally.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google No one, not even Todd McFarlane, was sure how Santa Claus would fit into the world of Spawn, but a year after the resounding success of I Saw Santa , the first Christmas-themed spinoff in the Spawn Universe, it's showing no signs of stopping. The second issue of the follow-up series, appropriately titled I Saw Spawn , will release on comic book store shelves on December 16, and they're just getting started. That doesn't mean that Todd was immediately convinced by it when he first heard it.

When asked by ComicBook if he'd ever considered what Santa was up to in the Spawn Universe before, given his previous appearances in countless other superhero universes, McFarlane simply replied, "No," with a laugh.

"I probably came in with my bar pretty low and my expectations going, 'Okay, Spawn and Santa, here we go.' But by the end of the pitch, (Chris Killian, co-writer) had convinced me because he surprised me on the story that he and Andrew had come up with."

ComicBook's own Chris Killian and his brother Andrew Sanders wrote both the original I Saw Santa and this year's I Saw Spawn together, finding the balance of Spawn universe grime with Christmas iconography in the right doses.

"I think it's just using that holiday cheer to make things scarier," Killian said. "When we did this, we didn't want a Violent Night , badass Santa Claus. We didn't want any of that sort of stuff. We really wanted classic Norman Rockwell, Coca-Cola Santa, like the most innocent of characters that you can think of because that's going to make what we do to them so much more horrifying."

For Killian and Sanders, there's no sibling rivalry or brotherly head-butting when they collaborate, with the latter adding, "Me and Chris have always been very close and supporting each other as much as possible…He graduated three or so years before me in high school, and he waited to go to college until I was ready to go, and then we both went together." Killian added, "My mom is always like, I don't know what I did that you guys get along so well, but I'm glad because she hates her siblings."

Though there aren't any arguments about where to take the story when they're writing, they still push each other. Killian credits his brother with the gruesome idea from I Saw Santa , where his reindeer have their hooves sliced off with razor wire, preventing Santa from escaping.

"I thought, no way, bro. We're not gonna do that," Killiand said. With a smile, Sanders added, "It took like five days to convince him….I try to throw some stuff out there that'll make him cringe or fight back."

For McFarlane, having something in the Spawn Universe that's distinct from the main title and its superhero DNA is important, and goes back to expanding the world with Sam and Twitch. That said, McFarlane says that expansions of the Spawn line need to maintain a Kevin Bacon-like rule, "You need to be like seven degrees away from (Spawn)."

Though the team won't divulge plans for the Santa-centric corner of the Spawn Universe, they did open up about how the naming convention for its future might shift. As fans may recall, Marvel got locked into their Spider-Man movies maintaining the world "Home" in all the titles. Will the Christmas side of Spawn maintain the "I Saw ____" titles as it moves forward?

"We haven't fully decided that yet," Killian said. "I personally don't think I would want to do I Saw blank every year. I don't think that's the route. It would probably be more to go back to I Saw Santa and then have a subtitle that changes every year. Would be my guess."

McFarlane added, "Chris and I have talked about this before, that it definitely has to look like a Christmas-themed book, right? Which is why the design on the books looks like it's Christmas wrapping and stuff. It has to scream, 'Hey, I'm a Christmas story. I'm over here.' Because it's too easy to get lost in the other 200 superhero books that are being racked right next to it, right? So we'll continue to try and brand it."

Spawn fans also know that McFarlane has been trying for years to get a new Spawn movie off the ground, but what about the potential for I Saw Santa on the big screen? McFarlane teased, "Those are conversations that are ongoing literally right now."

"I was having that conversation with Chris, that it could kind of work if I get this one thing going, or we just take some of the Spawn elements out, and I think I Saw Santa could be its own thing, a standalone, because it's just cool of all the characters that they have in there. So I think we could go either way."

I Saw Spawn #2 will arrive in comic book stores on December 16.

articles.title: Someone Asked Jenna Ushkowitz About The Online ‘Glee Curse’ Chatter After So Many People Have Died
articles.summary: The Ryan Murphy show is associated with a number of real-life tragedies.
articles.content:
Shortly it debuted back in 2009, Ryan Murphy 's campy musical comedy Glee became a sensation. The series (which is streaming with a Hulu subscription) broke barriers in regards to LGBTQ+ representation, and also featured plenty of memorable musical numbers . The show has also been associated with a number of tragedies, with three main cast members having died, starting with Cory Monteith's death back in 2013. There's been chatter online about the " Glee curse" and now Tina actress Jenna Ushkowitz has issued a heartfelt response about that discourse.

Talk about honesty. While folks online might be talking about the show's curse with levity, the experience of those who actually worked on Glee is another one entirely. Real people died, not characters, which has been a source for quite a bit of pain by the rest of the cast. Those feelings remain to this day, case in point being Harry Shum Jr. honoring Naya Rivera this season on Dancing with the Stars .

The internet can be a cruel place, and the discourse about the Glee curse has clearly been painful for the cast. The tragic loss of their coworkers is hard enough, but the light-hearted chatter about these deaths has clearly created more pain for the members of the William McKinley High School Glee Club. Hopefully Ushkowitz's comments will circulate online, and help to quiet that type of talk.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google It's an absolute no-brainer that Warner Bros. would have at least met with David Fincher about a Batman movie . He is, after all, a director known for darkness and urban crime , and as he confirmed on the Happy Sad Confused podcast , there was a meeting. It was, as he describes it, a brief one, as his suggestions might have been too dark. "Batman was, you know, they asked me, and I was kind of like, 'I mean, if this, this, this,' and they were like, 'Thank you very much.'" he said. When pressed on what those "Ifs" were, he pivoted to the movie that ultimately did employ most of them.

"I think what Matt [Reeves] did with the last one was kind of what I was pitching in 19-whatever," he said. "It's just about how sinister and how brackish we could we could make that world." Considering that Paul Dano's version of the Riddler, and the grimy urban Gotham, reminded many viewers of Fincher's Seven , this should hardly come as a surprise.

Fincher's further explanation comes with a bit of historical irony, though. "Remember when Tim Burton's movie came out, people thought it was dark, you know, you look at it now, it looks like, I mean, you could buy that wallpaper at Kmart. It is like the Adam West, it's colorful, it's playful." At the time, of course, Burton's 1989 movie was meant to be a clean break from the campy '60s Batman, with fans initially protesting the casting of Michael Keaton because he was known as a comedian. Burton's vision, however, was arguably no more realistic, with its German expressionist and noir roots every it as stylized as the Bif! Pow! Zap! of the TV show. After noting that he doesn't think anyone has ever really gotten Batman perfect, though, David Fincher pays respect to the '89 version after all when asked who the best Batman is.

"I think the best Batman has been Michael Keaton because what he really did with…that first movie worked for me because of Michael Keaton saying, when he's trying to explain…You're seeing this is the psychotic break and the guy's trying, and I've always loved that. I've always thought that was, you know, I had high hopes for Val Kilmer and I was like, 'What the f**k?' Well, that was the wrong fit. I love Val Kilmer. I mean, don't get me wrong, but wrong." For a director whose reputation is one of specificity and perfectionism, his word choice is a bit all-over, but this is the scene Fincher seems to be talking about in regards to Keaton:

With DC Studios now seeming to operate by the unwritten guideline of whether grandma would like it, Fincher probably won't get asked to do a Batman film again any time soon. James Gunn was seemingly moving towards a Bat-family concept with The Brave and the Bold , fitting his usual formula of superheroes as broken people who make found families. After many years of Batman as loner, a lot of merchandise money has been left on the table for the likes of Robin, Nightwing, Batgirl, and all the rest. A safer, more paternal Batman is most likely in the cards now.

Would you rather see a David Fincher Batman, though? Leave us your manifesto on the subject in comments.

Anticipation is high for the upcoming Marvel movie , especially because Doomsday' s cast list includes entire teams of superheroes. That includes Channing Tatum 's Gambit, who is clarifying comments about toning down his character's accent .

Honestly, this tracks. Tatum's Doomsday Dunkin' Ad featured him with Gambit's signature accent, and it was easy enough to understand the mutant as he spoke to H.E.R.B.I.E. about the coffee company's seasonal treats. He's still going to be using the Cajun dialect, but won't be going so far as to use Cajun French throughout the course of the Avengers movie's runtime.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Idris Elba may be best known for playing tremendous characters in the MCU, HBO's The Wire , and his BBC detective John Luther , but his career extends far beyond just what you see on the screen. Fans may know that he dabbles in music and kickboxing too, but Elba has made a name for himself behind the camera too. In 2018, Elba made his directorial debut with Yardie , and this year he returns to the director's chair with the new sci-fi thriller film, Above the Below .

Elba isn't just behind the camera, though he's in front of it for Above the Below . Plus, he's alone in his directorial duties, though, as he co-directed the film with Martin Owen ( The Loneliest Boy in the World, The Intergalactic Adventures of Max Cloud ). Speaking with ComicBook ahead of the film's release, the pair broke down how they worked as co-directors, revealing that the process happened naturally with minimal creative disagreements.

"I'll be really honest," Elba said. "Not to be cheesy or corny, but we didn't really have disagreements and we really didn't have delegated areas. We both chipped in on all areas at any time. Some meetings Martin would lead because he had an interesting perspective on it, and it was never jarring to me. We met each other on the Zoom, and the first day we actually wearing very similar outfits, black T-shirts and a bit of little beanie. And it was from there we realized that we had similar ambitions for the film."

Owen added that was never a conversation between the two of them about how pieces of the directing job would delegated between them. "We found it naturally," he said. "I think we found that rhythm, found who likes to focus on this, who likes to focus on that. And it just works really, really well."

In jest, Elba added, "But I did most of the work though," prompting Owen to add, "I turned up a couple of days, but most of the time I was just I was in the hotel."

We also asked Elba if he had any interest in returning to the franchises that he'd previously acted in and bringing his directing skills to them. The star had two that immediately came to mind, and one of them seems like it could happen very soon.

"Just because I've been with this character for the longest time is John Luther. Like, I would like to direct an installment of that, and hopefully one day will," Elba said. "I would love… Man, I did a film called Hobbs and Shaw, and I played in that film, a character called Brixton Lore. I loved Brixton. I wouldn't mind bringing him back, I tell you that."

Above the Below arrives in theaters on December 4.

articles.title: Batman Annual 2026 #1 Builds Up Not One, But Two Villains who Grapple for Control of Gotham (Review)
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics The Minotaur has been stalking Gotham City for months now. Ever since the beginning of Matt Fraction's run, this fourteen-fingered villain has hung over Gotham City like a shadow, pulling strings and manipulating events to always go his way. The most dangerous part is that Batman didn't even notice, falling right into the Minotaur's algorithm […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The Minotaur has been stalking Gotham City for months now. Ever since the beginning of Matt Fraction's run, this fourteen-fingered villain has hung over Gotham City like a shadow, pulling strings and manipulating events to always go his way. The most dangerous part is that Batman didn't even notice, falling right into the Minotaur's algorithm of crime as it slowly entrenched itself into every facet of Gotham. Now, with the release of Batman Annual 2026 #1, we finally catch a glimpse of just who the Minotaur is underneath his mask, and the exact kind of threat he poses to Batman's city.

The biggest revelation, however, is that he isn't the ultimate mastermind. There's another threat that's been lurking in the shadows since the beginning, and we're finally seeing his own goals begin to come into the light. The Minotaur is running the show, but the legendarily underexplored Calculator is writing the script, and the Minotaur has no idea that he's playing right into his hands. This issue, written by Matt Fraction, with two different stories featuring art by Brian Ching and Jesse Lonergan, respectively, is a great villain-focused issue that this run definitely needed, and it has me more than excited for the next issues of Batman (2025).

This issue was comprised of two stories. The first focused on the Minotaur's first days and rise to power in Gotham, showing how he was a talented businessman who excelled at extracting the maximum profit from targets before leaving them high and dry. He got into the crime game for a real challenge, having seen what he believes could be a perfect algorithm for crime. He wants to master crime in Gotham simply to prove that he can, and leave his mark on the world. To that end, he recruited the Calculator to make his vision a reality. Unbeknownst to him, the Calculator is using him for his own plans. He knows that Batman will inevitably stop the Minotaur, and he's going to use that to prove his own equation for reality and escape with the greatest heist of all.

This gave us some much-needed character building and context for the Minotaur, and it's very smart in how it approaches him. The Minotaur, at the end of the day, is a Batman villain, and everyone knows what one of those looks like. This story doesn't go out of its way to try and show us why the Minotaur is smarter or better or different from the other dozens of villains we've seen, instead simply showing us who he is and why he's doing this. The Minotaur's sheer charisma and unique perspective sell him enough on their own. He's not something we haven't seen before , but he is a well-designed villain with a gimmick that Batman hasn't faced before, and that's enough.

Where things get really interesting, however, is with the Calculator. He's never been a villain with much of an identity beyond wanting to contrast Oracle, but this single issue reinvigorates him with a brand-new direction. Even that direction itself draws on everything that makes Batman's stories work and uses that. It doesn't pretend that Batman won't win in the end, but acknowledges that, and instead refocuses the tension on the Calculator's attempt to get as rich as he can and escape before that happens. This entire run has been about moving the goalpost in fun, invigorating ways to increase the tension and bring down the stakes, and this issue is a perfect example of just how it's been doing that.

Brian Ching penciled the main story, with Adriano Lucas on colors, and they were a clear power team. Ching's style is rough but highly tuned towards action, giving everything a gritty impact that shines whenever the Minotaur rips through an enemy, or Batman stands like a spectre of looming defeat. Lucas's colors ground everything in an eerie atmosphere, making fantastic use of background colors like red and orange to put Gotham City's darker side on full display. My favorite page in the entire book has to be the beautiful shot of the Minotaur and Calculator looking at the burning Gotham, which perfectly combines the art and colors to make something incredible.

Jesse Lonergan handled art and colors for the Calculator-focused backup, and the paneling here is nothing short of inspired. The script revolves around the Calculator's obsession with the golden ratio, and the pages themselves are segmented to reflect that. The layout of these pages is incredibly creative and beautiful to look at. My favorite of the bunch might just be the Two-Face pages, with different panels stacked on top of each other to represent his distinct halves. There are so many little things to love on these pages, and while the Calculator himself goes through too many face changes across them for my liking, this setup is impressive on just about every level, and I loved it.

Which of these villains do you think will give Batman the worst run for his money? Let us know in the comments below!
